nodes.summary: The number at risk at `time j`: subjects whose observation time is at least `time j`.
nodes.title: Number at risk at an observation time

nodes.summary: Right-censored survival data grouped at `k` distinct, increasing observation times: `deaths j` subjects die and `censored j` subjects are censored at `time j`.
nodes.title: Grouped right-censored survival data

nodes.summary: The deaths at a time are among those at risk.
nodes.title: Deaths at a time are among those at risk

nodes.summary: The Kaplan–Meier factor is at most `1`.
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier factor is at most one

nodes.summary: The Kaplan–Meier factor is non-negative.
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier factor is nonnegative

nodes.summary: The Kaplan–Meier factor `1 - dⱼ / nⱼ` at `time j` (it is `1` if nobody is at risk, where also `dⱼ = 0`).
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier factor

nodes.summary: The Kaplan–Meier jumps are non-negative.
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier jumps are nonnegative

nodes.summary: The Kaplan–Meier jump at `time j`: `Ŝ(tⱼ₋) · dⱼ / nⱼ`.
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier jump at an observation time

nodes.summary: The Kaplan–Meier measure is a probability measure.
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier measure is a probability measure

nodes.summary: The mass of a measurable set under the Kaplan–Meier measure.
nodes.title: Mass of a set under the Kaplan–Meier measure

nodes.summary: The survival function of the Kaplan–Meier measure is the Kaplan–Meier estimate on `(-∞, τ)`: `P(T > t) = Ŝ(t)` for `t < τ`.
nodes.title: Survival function of the Kaplan–Meier measure

nodes.summary: The Kaplan–Meier measure: the jumps `kmMass j` at `time j` and the leftover mass `kmTail` at a chosen point `τ` (taken after the last observation time).
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier measure

nodes.summary: Without censoring, the Kaplan–Meier estimate is the empirical survival function: the fraction `#{observations > t} / n = 1 - Fₙ(t)`.
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier estimate without censoring is the empirical survival

nodes.summary: A time at which some subject is censored has positive Kaplan–Meier survival.
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier survival is positive at a censoring time

nodes.summary: The Kaplan–Meier estimate `Ŝ(t) = ∏_{tⱼ ≤ t} (1 - dⱼ / nⱼ)` of the survival function.
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier survival estimate

nodes.summary: The leftover Kaplan–Meier mass is non-negative.
nodes.title: Leftover Kaplan–Meier mass is nonnegative

nodes.summary: The Kaplan–Meier mass left after the last observation time, `∏ⱼ (1 - dⱼ / nⱼ)`.
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier mass after the last observation

nodes.summary: Kaplan–Meier is the nonparametric MLE (Kaplan–Meier 1958): every probability measure on `ℝ` has censored-data likelihood at most that of the Kaplan–Meier measure.
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier is the nonparametric MLE

nodes.summary: The censored-data likelihood of a law `μ` of the survival time: `∏ⱼ μ{tⱼ}^{dⱼ} · μ(tⱼ, ∞)^{cⱼ}`.
nodes.title: Likelihood of right-censored data

nodes.summary: Self-consistency (Efron 1967, (7.4)): `n Ŝ(t)` is the number of observations exceeding `t` plus, for each subject censored at or before `t`, the conditional survival `Ŝ(t) / Ŝ(tⱼ)`.
nodes.title: Self-consistency

nodes.summary: The number of subjects in the sample.
nodes.title: Sample size of censored survival data

nodes.summary: The Kaplan–Meier jumps and the leftover mass add up to `1`.
nodes.title: Kaplan–Meier jumps and leftover mass sum to one

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
